C-UPDATER-REVIEW-FIXES.Summary: The 2026-11-02 smart review of the 2.9.x-next train (base v2.8.2 3b6d49e4, head f3d88851) found four blocking defects in the C-UPDATER-ROLLBACK restore paths, two further rollback-integrity defects (an instance-lock race and a false-success CLI outcome), and three defects that leave the C-UPDATER-STATS gateway unable to record or read live numbers; all nine were re-verified against the code on 2026-11-02. This change fixes exactly those nine defects plus the two stale file-local contract links, and ships the M-068/M-071 graph and verification deltas. Nothing else changes: the counting routes stay byte-identical and no client or renderer code is touched.
C-UPDATER-REVIEW-FIXES.Problem: (1) GUI restore mutates preferences before verification: m068_rollback.rs:1010 calls replace_from_snapshot before the staged-bundle digest check (lines 1014-1020) and before the bundle swap, so a digest mismatch aborts with settings already replaced — the "aborting untouched" message at line 1019 is then false; a corrupt snapshot reaches m005_prefs load_from (m005_prefs.rs:262), which substitutes an empty map on invalid JSON and can wipe live settings. (2) Windows CLI restores preferences before verification: m068_rollback.rs:672 writes the snapshot and skippedUpdateVersion before the feed fetch (line 676), the version check and the minisignature verification, so a network or signature failure returns an error with settings already changed — despite the in-code comment "prefs + skip writes LAST before spawn" at lines 669-671. The Windows GUI path shares the defect: mt_rollback_restore performs the unconditional preferences restore at line 1010 before restore_inner's fetch and verification run, and passes a no-op prefs_write closure into restore_inner (line 1049, "already restored above"), so the dialog-initiated restore also mutates settings before verification. (3) macOS half-swap: both the CLI (m068_rollback.rs:639-644) and the GUI (1028-1029) trash the running bundle before renaming the staged bundle into place; a rename failure leaves the application path empty. (4) Unsafe promotion: m068_rollback.rs:415-429 validates staging by JSON parse and version compare only, then deletes the live set before the promotion rename succeeds; an invalid manifest can become the live set and a filesystem failure destroys the only remaining restore path. (5) The gateway writes an invalid datapoint: worker.mjs:94 passes index (singular) to env.STATS.writeDataPoint, which accepts indexes: [value]; the local mock (tests/tools/stats-gateway.test.mjs:115) pins the wrong field. (6) The live SQL selects a non-existent column: query.mjs:119 selects index AS event, but Analytics Engine sample rows expose index1. (7) A successful live response prints empty: query.mjs:130 reads json.result while SQL API rows arrive in json.data. (8) Instance-lock race in the CLI: m068_rollback.rs:872 uses try_acquire_instance_lock as a probe whose guard is dropped at the end of the if statement — before the re-acquire at line 889 — then re-acquires there; when that second acquisition fails, the error is silently ignored and the restore proceeds under a possibly live instance. (9) CLI false success: m068_rollback.rs:657-659 ignores a relaunch error, deletes the staging directory and returns event=restored, although R-5 defines exit 0 as "restored and relaunched". Additionally the LINKS blocks at m068_rollback.rs:19 and worker.mjs:22 point at .grace/graph/runtime.xml although the routes M-068 and M-071 live in .grace/graph/features.xml, and both label already-archived changes as active.

Goals.Goal: Make every restore path verify-then-mutate, per the M-068 Contract Purpose "a restore re-verifies everything before touching the system" and C-UPDATER-ROLLBACK R-3: "a digest mismatch aborts with the current state untouched"; on macOS "the bundle swap strictly precedes both writes"; on Windows the preferences and skip writes are "the last writes before the spawn", after verification. The GUI restore must verify the digest and parse the snapshot as a valid object before any preferences mutation or swap; the Windows CLI must perform the feed fetch, version check and minisignature verification before writing preferences.

Make the macOS bundle replacement reversible, per R-3 "never a half-swap": the current bundle is renamed aside first and returns to the running path on any failure before the replacement confirms, so no failure leaves the application path empty (Trash moves the departed bundle only after the confirmed swap, per Criterion 3).

Make boot promotion atomic, per R-1 "promote-only-after-success" (referenced by R-3): staging is validated (strict manifest plus artifact digests) and the previous live set survives until the replacement rename succeeds, so neither an invalid manifest nor a filesystem failure destroys the restore path.

Make the gateway wire format real: worker.mjs writes indexes: [index] (the event as a single-element indexes array) in the documented writeDataPoint shape; query.mjs live mode selects index1 and reads rows from json.data; tests pin both documented Cloudflare shapes; the M-071 datapoint output contract is updated to the wire form.

Hold the CLI instance lock for the process lifetime: the first successfully acquired guard is kept (no probe-then-reacquire gap), per the R-5 probe intent "no headless swap under a running app, no second process"; a lock that cannot be held aborts restore work.

Make the CLI outcome truthful, per the R-5 exit table "0 restored and relaunched": a relaunch failure after a successful restore is reflected in the machine-readable outcome and in printed guidance for starting the restored app, not reported as plain success.
Restore file-local contract truth: the LINKS blocks in m068_rollback.rs and worker.mjs reference .grace/graph/features.xml and name archived changes as archived.

Constraints.Constraint: Counting stays best-effort per the M-071 Contract: "a binding failure changes no response"; the /feed and /pkg routes keep byte-identical behavior (paths, validation, 302 targets, 404 policy).
No client or renderer code changes; the tauri.conf.json endpoints array and the C-UPDATER-ROLLBACK direct-GitHub restore fetches stay as designed (M-071 Dependencies).

Every order-of-operations and wire-shape failure mode fixed here gets a regression test; the review found that the existing rollback suite (19 tests under the plan's filter) and 18 gateway tests do not cover these failures.
No owner credentials in tests or CI: live Analytics Engine proof remains an owner-side manual step; tests use documented shapes and fixtures only.

The mark-site edit (T-012) is a sibling-repository write following the C-UPDATER-STATS pattern: a task-level ../mark-site path outside ObservedWriteScope, assuming the wave worktree sits beside the mark-site checkout; the site deploy stays owner-executed.

The draft C-STATS-READOUT change shares worker.mjs, query.mjs and tests/tools/stats-gateway.test.mjs with this change; this change lands first and C-STATS-READOUT rebases on it, because its readout route runs the same SQL this change repairs.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Renderer findings 11-14 of the review (Reveal async error loss, rollback-confirm promise loss, false clipboard-success pulse, English-only rollback error message) — deferred.

Three pre-existing defects beyond the nine, deferred as one explicitly tracked rollback-integrity follow-up: the GUI's lockless start when the CLI already holds the instance lock (main.rs:717-720 has no else branch); the delegation ack written before the dialog emit (m068_rollback.rs:786-802, which makes R-5's exit-6 broken-dialog path unreachable); and R-3's Windows pending-window serialization ("a staging-area lock or marker"), which was never implemented — the M-068 graph Summary's "the staging lock serialize everything" claim is false today and T-010 removes it rather than leaving the graph lying.
Wave A progressive-mount findings — out of the 2.9.x-next train per the owner decision.
No redesign of the rollback UX, no new gateway routes, no live deploy step in this change.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: GUI restore (mt_rollback_restore) verifies before mutating on both platforms, through a testable seam (the restore core extracted with a root override, the restore_inner precedent at m068_rollback.rs:561): on macOS the snapshot is parsed as a valid preferences object and the staged-bundle digest re-verified and the swap completed before the preferences write, and a post-swap preferences failure is logged and non-blocking (R-3 parity with the CLI's prefs_skipped); on Windows the unconditional line-1010 write is gone and the real preferences write rides inside restore_inner after the feed, version and minisignature verification as the last write before the spawn (the no-op prefs_write closure is removed); digest-mismatch and corrupt-snapshot cases leave preferences and bundle byte-identical, proven by regression tests.

Windows CLI writes the snapshot and skippedUpdateVersion after the staging write and before the spawn's final re-digest (final order: fetch, verify, stage, prefs write, re-digest, spawn — the re-digest stays the last step before execution, satisfying both R-3 clauses literally; today the preferences write at m068_rollback.rs:672 precedes both fetches, the verification and the staging); each failure path — feed fetch error, installer fetch error, version disagreement, signature failure, staging write failure — has a test asserting preferences are unchanged.

An injected macOS swap failure before the replacement rename confirms restores the departed bundle to the running path; the aside uses a deterministic sibling name, and the shared swap routine takes the target bundle path as a parameter (injectable for tests, which have no .app ancestor). The two crash windows are stated honestly: a hard crash between the two renames leaves the running path empty and the departed bundle at the deterministic aside name — recovery there is one manual rename, the only possible mechanism since Mark itself cannot boot to reconcile an empty path; a crash after the replacement rename leaves a stale aside that the next boot's reconciliation removes (the path is occupied, so Mark boots). No state leaves the system without a recoverable bundle at a known path. A Trash failure after a confirmed swap is logged and non-blocking (R-3).

Boot promotion validates the staging manifest before any mutation (manifest-shape invalidity discards the staging without hashing, live set survives), re-verifies artifact digests only on the promotion path before its rename (a digest mismatch there also discards the staging, live set surviving; the discard-only branch hashes nothing), and keeps the previous live set until that rename confirms via its own move-aside in the data root — a rename onto the non-empty live directory is impossible on the filesystems in question; at boot, reconciliation covers both stale asides with a fail-closed rule: a stale bundle aside with the running path occupied is trashed, a stale promotion aside with a valid live set is deleted (remove_dir_all — the data root carries no Trash semantics; R-6's bounded footprint is preserved, the transient peak equals today's staging window, and the confirmed old set is freed in the same reconcile call, not parked in the user's Trash), a stale promotion aside with a missing or invalid live set is promoted back when its own manifest passes validation and is deleted otherwise (it can never become live — bounded footprint, logged); a foreign or symlinked aside (anything at an aside name that is not a directory holding a valid set: symlink, file or garbage) skips only its own reconciliation branch with a log line — never wedging boot or the rest of reconciliation; deletion applies only to the data-root promotion aside (Mark's own directory), never to a foreign object in the bundle's parent (a shared system directory where a name collision is someone else's content — left in place and logged, covered by the FAQ's manual-recovery command); a bundle aside with the running path empty is renamed back — a defensive branch for the transient lockless-GUI window, exercised in tests, while the user-facing recovery for that window stays the documented manual rename — and a promote-back runs only after the aside's own manifest passes the same strict validation and its artifact digests re-hash clean (the same threshold as promotion; the manifest check applies to promotion asides — a bundle aside is valid when it is a directory whose Contents/MacOS/mark is a regular file (checked via symlink_metadata — exists()/is_dir() follow symlinks); an invalid manifest never becomes live, reconciliation included); the covering tests exercise reconcile_at_boot itself through a root-override seam (invalid manifest, digest mismatch, injected rename failure, both stale-aside cases), not only the decision table.

worker.mjs passes the event as a single-element indexes array (indexes: [index] in count()'s current naming); the gateway tests assert the exact documented writeDataPoint shape; the M-071 datapoint output contract and the tests are updated in the same change (worker, tests and graph delta land in one PR).

query.mjs live mode selects index1 AS event and reads rows from json.data; a live-format response fixture prints both tables (day x event x OS/platform and from-version breakdown) correctly — a new live-format test.
The CLI keeps its first successfully acquired instance-lock guard until process exit; when the lock cannot be held, no restore work is performed (test covers the failed-acquisition path).

An injected relaunch failure after a successful macOS restore produces the machine-readable outcome event=restored_norelaunch (a new MARK_ROLLBACK token; the M-068 dictionary extension ships in this change's graph delta) with exit code 6 — R-5's failure row, whose detail now carries this case — plus printed guidance naming the restored application path, while the restored bundle remains in place; no path reports plain restored when the relaunch did not happen.

The LINKS blocks in m068_rollback.rs, worker.mjs, query.mjs and tests/tools/stats-gateway.test.mjs are made true: graph links point at .grace/graph/features.xml, verification links at .grace/verification/features.xml (V-M-068/V-M-071's actual home — .grace/verification/runtime.xml has never carried them), and the already-archived changes are named as archived; grace lint for this change reports zero errors in this change's files (the three pre-existing module-map errors in the abandoned .claude/worktrees/split-scroll-sync-restore worktree are baseline noise outside this change's scope, unchanged by it).

VerificationIntent.ExpectedCommand: cargo test --bin mark rollback; npx vitest run tests/tools/stats-gateway.test.mjs; grace lint --path . --change C-UPDATER-REVIEW-FIXES --assertions target (during implementation); grace lint --path . --change C-UPDATER-REVIEW-FIXES --assertions final --run-commands (before archiving)
VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: New order-of-operations and wire-format regression tests pass; the existing rollback suite (19 tests today under the plan's cargo test --bin mark rollback filter: 16 in m068_rollback plus the 3 CLI flag tests in m020_cli) and the 18 gateway tests stay green; grace lint zero errors attributable to this change's files (the pre-existing worktree noise excluded); M-068/M-071 graph deltas and V-M-068/V-M-071 verification updates ship in the same change.

Assumptions.Assumption: Review facts were re-verified by direct code read on 2026-11-02 at f3d88851: the four rollback blockers (m068_rollback.rs lines 639-644, 672, 1010, 1028-1029), the instance-lock race (872-889), the relaunch-error path (657-659) and the worker.mjs index field are confirmed as described.

Cloudflare Analytics Engine writeDataPoint accepts {indexes, blobs, doubles}, sample rows expose the index1 column, and SQL API responses carry rows in data — per the official documentation; without live credentials the actual behavior of today's wrong field is unproven either way and is not claimed.

The draft C-STATS-READOUT (whose summary now says "counting by design", naming this change as its prerequisite) depends on this change landing first; no claim about live counting behavior is made or depended on either way.

reconcile_at_boot gains a root-override seam in this change (the restore_inner precedent at m068_rollback.rs:561), so the promotion test exercises the real boot path against a temp root rather than re-stating its decision table.
